source_ref: Class 10 Physics - original one-line definitions and structured facts.

items.definition: The bouncing back of light rays when they strike a smooth polished surface.
The bending of light when it passes obliquely from one transparent medium into another.

items.term: Principal focus of a concave mirror
items.definition: The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis converge after reflection.
The point inside a lens through which a ray of light passes without any deviation.
The ability of a lens to converge or diverge light rays, measured as the reciprocal of its focal length in metres.
The rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-section of a conductor.
The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another.
At constant temperature, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends.
The property of a conductor that opposes the flow of current through it.
The resistance of a conductor of unit length and unit cross-sectional area; it depends only on the material.
The rate at which electrical energy is consumed in a circuit.
The region around a magnet or a current-carrying conductor in which its magnetic influence can be felt.
The production of an induced current in a coil due to a change in the magnetic field linked with it.
The splitting of white light into its constituent colours.
The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length to see both near and distant objects clearly.
The minimum distance at which an object is seen most clearly by a normal eye, about 25 cm.

items.subject: Concave mirror
items.attribute: type of image for a distant object
items.value: Real, inverted and highly diminished at the focus

items.subject: Convex mirror
items.value: Virtual, erect and diminished

items.subject: Convex mirror
items.value: Rear-view mirrors in vehicles

items.subject: Concave mirror
items.value: Shaving and dentist's mirrors, torch reflectors, solar furnaces

items.subject: Convex lens
items.value: Converging lens

items.subject: Concave lens
items.value: Diverging lens

items.subject: Object at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror
items.value: At the centre of curvature, same size, real and inverted

items.subject: Retina
items.value: Acts as a screen on which the image is formed; contains light-sensitive cells

items.subject: Iris
items.value: Controls the size of the pupil and hence the amount of light entering the eye

items.subject: Ciliary muscles
items.value: Change the focal length of the eye lens

items.subject: Optic nerve
items.value: Carries visual information from the retina to the brain

items.subject: Cornea
items.value: Provides most of the refraction of light entering the eye

items.subject: Myopia (short-sightedness)
items.value: Concave lens of suitable power

items.subject: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness)
items.value: Convex lens of suitable power

items.subject: Presbyopia
items.value: Bifocal lens

items.subject: Myopia
items.value: Excessive curvature of the cornea or elongation of the eyeball

items.subject: Hypermetropia
items.value: Focal length of the eye lens too long or the eyeball too small

items.subject: Twinkling of stars
items.value: Atmospheric refraction of starlight

items.subject: Advance sunrise and delayed sunset
items.value: About 4 minutes (2 minutes each)

items.subject: Blue colour of the sky
items.value: Scattering of light by air molecules (shorter wavelengths scatter more)

items.subject: Red colour of the sun at sunrise and sunset
items.value: Scattering of shorter wavelengths over a long atmospheric path, so red light reaches us

items.subject: Danger signals
items.value: Red, because it scatters the least and travels farthest through fog and smoke

items.subject: Rainbow
items.value: Dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight by water droplets

items.subject: Prism dispersion
items.value: Red

items.subject: Prism dispersion
items.value: Violet

items.subject: Newton
items.value: Showed that white light is made of seven colours using a prism

items.subject: SI unit of electric current
items.value: ampere (A)

items.subject: SI unit of potential difference
items.value: volt (V)

items.subject: SI unit of resistance
items.value: ohm (Ω)

items.subject: SI unit of electric charge
items.value: coulomb (C)

items.subject: SI unit of electric power
items.value: watt (W)

items.subject: SI unit of resistivity
items.value: ohm metre (Ω m)

items.subject: Commercial unit of electrical energy
items.value: kilowatt hour (kWh)

items.subject: Ammeter
items.value: In series; it has very low resistance

items.subject: Voltmeter
items.value: In parallel; it has very high resistance

items.subject: Filament of an electric bulb
items.value: Tungsten, because of its high melting point and high resistivity

items.subject: Electric heater element
items.value: Nichrome, because it has high resistivity and does not oxidise readily

items.subject: Live wire
items.value: Red (or brown)

items.subject: Neutral wire
items.value: Black (or blue)

items.subject: Earth wire
items.value: Green (or green-yellow)

items.subject: Magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet
items.value: From the north pole to the south pole

items.subject: Magnetic field lines
items.value: They never intersect each other

items.subject: Magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor
items.value: Concentric circles centred on the wire

items.subject: Magnetic field inside a solenoid
items.value: Uniform and parallel, like that of a bar magnet

items.subject: Right-hand thumb rule
items.value: Direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor

items.subject: Fleming's left-hand rule
items.value: Direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor)

items.subject: Fleming's right-hand rule
items.value: Direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field (generator)

items.subject: Electric motor
items.value: Electrical energy into mechanical energy

items.subject: Electric generator
items.value: Mechanical energy into electrical energy

items.subject: Split-ring commutator
items.value: Reverses the direction of current in the coil every half rotation

items.subject: Electromagnet
items.value: Soft iron, because it loses magnetism quickly when the current is switched off

items.subject: Fuse
items.value: Protects appliances by melting and breaking the circuit when the current exceeds a safe value

items.subject: Short circuit
items.value: Live and neutral wires come into direct contact, so resistance becomes very low and current very high

items.subject: Oersted
items.value: Showed that an electric current produces a magnetic field around it
